entry.title: Show HN: Ghost Runner - Race your past self on Apple Watch (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
entry.summary: Making running somewhat of a routine has the side effect of repeating the same routes very often. As someone raised playing games like Sega Rally or Collin McRae Rally, I found myself thinking of racing against the ghost of a previous run, and that's how the idea for Ghost Runner came to be. As a semi-retired developer now playing with the new tools of the trade, I put this together (aka iterated with Claude over 12 weeks and about 300 km of runs), and this is what came out. The biggest challenges were getting the zoom levels and transitions right as you race against up to 6 past versions of you and different performances, as well as the map detail in a way that would work for both road and trail runs. I'm proud of it and would love for some of you to test it as well and have fun with it. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50442219 Points: 1 # Comments: 0

entry.title: Show HN: Ziperu is rubyzip with a Rust core, same API but faster and safer (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
entry.summary: Annoyed by slow zip handling in Ruby apps in gems like roo and caxlsx, they use rubyzip underneath which is pure Ruby and does a lot of per entry work in Ruby objects which is slow. My project keeps the rubyzip API (Zip::File, Zip::InputStream, etc.) but does the parsing compression and file IO in Rust, using the zip crate via magnus/rb-sys. Change a line in your gemfile and I ship precompiled gems so no Rust toolchain to install. About 6x faster reading lots of small entries, and 2x faster deflating big ones. It also adds a few things rubyzip doesn't have like limits for zip bombs, an open mode that doesn't modify the archive, and multithreaded compression. To check I didn't break anything, I run rubyzip's own test suite against it (416 of 476 pass; most of the rest test rubyzip internals), fuzz it against Python's zipfile, and run the test suites of roo, caxlsx, rubyXL and a few others with ziperu swapped in, working pretty well so far. I would love to hear ideas for new features, or zip edge cases that annoy you! Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50442141 Points: 1 # Comments: 0

entry.title: Show HN: Git-dupe - plain Git per-project private versioning for agent files (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
entry.summary: Hi HN! Suppose you have notes, skills, and agent instructions that are part of your personal workflow, so you do not want them committed to the public repo, but at the same time, you want them to be in the workspace at the correct locations (e.g., AGENTS.md file locations matter), and these files cannot be simply gitignored because you also want versioning for them. The solution to this is actually just a bit more plain Git. $ git status --short # public repo ?? AGENTS.md ?? notes/ $ git dupe init # private repo Initialized empty Git repository in /home/brian/code/project/.git/dupe/ $ git dupe add notes/ AGENTS.md # private repo hint: notes is now hidden from the project's Git; run from the root, 'git dupe unhide -- notes' stops hiding it $ git dupe commit -m "Notes and agent instructions" # private repo [main (root-commit) 3eb3af9] Notes and agent instructions 3 files changed, 3 insertions(+) create mode 100644 .gitdupe create mode 100644 AGENTS.md create mode 100644 notes/todo.md $ git status --short # public repo: nothing $ git dupe log --oneline # private repo: your files 3eb3af9 Notes and agent instructions The solution, in short, is versioning those agent files in a repo, say (this repo is private to you and holds the history for your agent files), and that repo shares the same worktree as the public repo . You essentially overlap the two, with put in .git/ (and .git/ is that of the public repo) for a convenient solution. If you want to read more about the strategy used, there is more comprehensive documentation in the repo. git-dupe supports macOS, Linux, and Windows and is under the MIT License. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50442093 Points: 1 # Comments: 0
